requirements.requirement: Provide the supplied project documents through a WebDAV workspace at /documents/ on node1 TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Apache was active and listening on port 8080; authenticated PROPFIND returned 207 and listed brief.txt and budget.csv. The same service and resources were observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: The editor account from access.txt can create, read, replace, and delete documents.
requirements.summary: Credentials extracted from access.txt authenticated successfully. Direct tests showed create PUT 201, matching GET, replacement PUT 204 with matching content, DELETE 204, and subsequent GET 404.

requirements.requirement: Honor exclusive document locks and prevent an update without the lock token from overwriting a locked document.
requirements.summary: An exclusive LOCK returned 200, a tokenless PUT returned 423, and a token-bearing PUT returned 204 with verified replacement content. Post-restart assertions repeated the lock behavior successfully.

requirements.requirement: Anonymous clients cannot access the workspace.
requirements.summary: Anonymous PROPFIND returned 401 both before and after the node restart, while authenticated PROPFIND succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the initial project documents in /srv/legacy2/webdav-document-locks.
requirements.summary: brief.txt and budget.csv remained at the required location with SHA-256 hashes identical to the authored baseline before testing, after CRUD/lock tests, and after restart. Test documents were deleted.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64. Apache 2.4.63 was installed from configured RHEL 10 repositories and demonstrated working DAV behavior before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the post-restart boot ID changed, and service, documents, authentication, CRUD-related write/delete behavior, firewall access, and locking recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the executor evidence.
limitations: Some credential-bearing command text and the post-restart tokenless/token-bearing PUT status values were redacted. Successful explicit assertions and the unredacted pre-restart lock test provide strong corroboration.

Lifecycle snapshots are bounded inventories and do not provide a comprehensive file or package delta; the retained /tmp/anon.body is directly visible, but other uncaptured minor residue cannot be excluded.
Requirement document-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: The task-related package, Apache, SELinux, firewall, ownership, and permission changes had clear roles, and final observations showed no failed services or damaged package-manager state. The only clearly unnecessary retained mutation was /tmp/anon.body, created during the anonymous-access probe and still present after execution; it was not cleaned up (cmd-96aa3ad0bbac4fbd). The successful package installation also used a one-time --nogpgcheck bypass after repository-key parsing failed; this directly enabled the required prerequisite and did not persistently disable verification, but it reduced package-integrity assurance for that transaction. The preceding failed install downloaded package cache entries that were reused by the successful installation, so it was not treated as unrelated residue.
